title: Fixed-sparsity-pattern approximation with relative Frobenius error.
summary: Approximate $A$ within the public support pattern $S$, using the comparison $\min_{B:S\circ B=B}\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$.

task.description_zh: Approximate $A$ within the public support pattern $S$, with comparison quantity $\min_{B:S\circ B=B}\|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}$.
description_paragraphs: Approximate $A$ within the public support pattern $S$, using the comparison $\min_{B:S\circ B=B}\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$.

model.instance: The unknown input is an arbitrary real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$. The public mask $S\in\{0,1\}^{d\times d}$ has exactly s ones in each row and column. The mask S constrains the output support, not the input A.

assumptions.description: Every row and column of S has exactly s ones. S is public instance data.

model.parameter_domain_description: Integers d>=1 and 1<=s<=d, with epsilon>0. The public mask may be part of the worst-case instance.
model.description_zh: The matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary. Every row and column of $S\in\{0,1\}^{d\times d}$ contains exactly $s$ ones, and $1\le s\le d$ holds. The operation $\circ$ denotes entrywise multiplication.

metric.normalization: If both numerator and denominator are zero, the loss is zero. A zero denominator with nonzero numerator gives +∞. Otherwise use the stated ratio.

metric.description_zh: Define $\|M\|_{\mathrm F}=(\sum_{ij}M_{ij}^2)^{1/2}$. The optimal error is $\operatorname{OPT}=\|A-S\circ A\|_{\mathrm F}$ and success requires $\|A-\widehat B\|_{\mathrm F}\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}$. Zero optimal error requires exact recovery.

bounds.derivation: The source Theorem 2 allows each row and column support size within a fixed proportional interval. Fixing its proportion to $1/2$ admits the subclass with exactly s entries per row and column. The native hard dimension is $d_0=s\lceil b_2/\varepsilon\rceil$. If $d\ge d_0+s$, extend it by an s-regular block-diagonal mask and a zero input block. Each extended left or right query is simulated by one corresponding native query. The lower bound takes the worst case over public masks.

proofs.title: Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task
proofs.body: Recover all $d$ columns by standard basis queries and return $S\circ A$. Every permitted entry is copied exactly and every prohibited entry is zero, so the output attains the best Frobenius residual for the public support pattern. The input need not follow that support pattern.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

proofs.title: General randomized adaptive two-sided queries and Wishart hard families.
proofs.body: Retain the cited primary theorem and include the padding argument here. Let d_0=s ceil(b_2/epsilon) be the native hard dimension. If d>=d_0+s, put r=d-d_0>=s. On an r by r block, choose the cyclic mask with s consecutive allowed positions in each row; it is s-regular in both rows and columns. Adjoin this mask block to the native hard mask and extend the hard input by a zero block. Every left or right query to the extended instance is simulated by one corresponding query to the native block. Restricting any admissible approximate output to the native block cannot increase its error, while the optimal masked approximation error is unchanged. The native lower bound therefore applies in the padded dimension.
